enumeration.method: Independent enumeration of complete printed THEOREM headings in pages 1-18 and the clipped main-text portion of page 19 finds exactly Theorems 1-4. Theorem 1 continues on page 10. The Appendix begins on the shared page 19 at y=313.6376953125; its heading is used only to establish the boundary. No appendix or embedded supplement body was used.

checks: Both the source-reviewed inventory and finalized census pass validation. The inventory hash matches its independent review, and every original claim field is preserved unchanged.
Title, five authors, arXiv v2 stamp dated 2 April 2024, versioned source URL, page count and PDF digest were checked. The heading-only crop verifies the shared-page Appendix cutoff.

All four complete Theorem statements were checked visually on pages 9,10,12,13,18: three phase branches, both bootstrap conclusions, the p-dimensional lower-orthant approximation and every sparse error term.

Simple-network conventions, independent-edge beta-model likelihood, the original jittering law, M(gamma;C_1), Condition 1, corrected edge functions and triangle moments/estimator were checked on pages 3-8.

The original lambda coefficients and the two variance components were checked on page 9, including ordered-pair sums, the factor 1/(2N), and N=(p-1)(p-2). Their combined variance was checked on pages 10-11.

The bootstrap sample law, doubly corrected edge functions, sample estimator, population moments, coefficients and combined population variance were checked on pages 11-12. The population center and variance are not replaced by conditional bootstrap or empirical versions.

Independent local-graph traversal confirms that Theorem 2 uses the bootstrap estimator but not original theta-hat, whereas Theorem 3 uses original theta-hat and population nu-dagger but not the bootstrap estimator itself.

The sparse beta-model, support, nonnegative effects, logarithmic residual reparametrization and linear sparse estimates were checked on pages 17-18. Theorem 4 has no dense Condition 1 or bootstrap dependency.

Twelve source-keyword groups retain nineteen separate original passages. Component passages are explicitly distinct rather than equivalent variants. Internal edges survive grouping; group reach was compared with independent local traversal.

Ten auxiliary passages resolve notation and population-law conventions; eighteen source notes retain the malformed membership, chi_p sign scope, error equality chain, log-domain omissions and other source ambiguities without repairing original statements.

All nineteen direct group/theorem uses and thirty-three related connections have matching paths, source explanations and selectors. Every selector matches its original passage/label or a related same-paper theorem.

source_notes: The audited source is the pinned arXiv v2 preprint; equality to final journal wording has not been established.

Theorem 1’s extra script-I membership and Theorem 4’s unparenthesized chi_p expression/equality chain remain exactly as printed. Source fidelity is not a certification of those statements as mathematically well posed.

Appendix and supplement references remain references. Proof-only expansions, the later adaptive-delta algorithm, empirical bootstrap variance estimation and applied confidence regions do not become theorem statement requirements.
Fixed s in Theorems 1/2, dimension p in Theorem 3 and growing sparse-support size s in Theorem 4 remain distinct.

Natural-language group titles use source keywords. Shared component grouping does not rewrite any original definition or claim mathematical equivalence between moments, estimators and variance quantities.

unresolved_source_references.description: Theorem 1 prints (alpha,beta) in script I in M(gamma;C_1). Script I denotes the edge-index set on page 4. This is an ill-typed or typographical membership chain, not a silently corrected hypothesis. Theorem 2 refers to the conditions of Theorem 1 and inherits this unresolved source wording.

Theorem 4 prints exp(-|xi^+| vee max_S |check-theta^+|) without grouping the maximum under the minus sign. Its intended negative-maximum interpretation is suggested by the subsequent chi_p^-1 discussion, but the original theorem formula is not repaired.

Theorem 4 writes the same rate expression as a literal equality between the intercept error and the maximum sparse-effect error. The preceding triangle inequalities justify bounds, not equality of those random errors. The printed chain is retained.

The source defines tilde-O_p through some sufficiently small fixed positive epsilon and a factor p^epsilon. It neither means only logarithmic factors nor explicitly quantifies every epsilon. This nonstandard convention is preserved.

The original and bootstrap moment estimators use logarithms of empirical ratios that may be zero, negative or undefined on finite-sample outcomes. No measurable fallback or truncation is specified. Asymptotic rates do not themselves define the estimator on all outcomes.

Noise variables are described as independent (and bootstrap noises iid), but independence from the original graph or the first sanitized graph is not separately stated. The conditional-flip identities and population-moment identities use fresh release noise. This implicit kernel interpretation is documented rather than added to quoted source statements.

The class M uses C_1<alpha,beta<0.5 and gamma=1-alpha-beta. It is empty when gamma>=1-2C_1, despite stating the nominal range gamma in (0,1]. The unnoised gamma=1 case discussed in remarks is outside this class.

Theorem 2 refers to the conditions of Theorem 1. Its own gamma window ranges across the three alternative phase branches; these branches are not simultaneous hypotheses. No Theorem-1 conclusion is imported as a new statement dependency.

Theorem 2 is printed as convergence of theta-hat-dagger centered at theta and normalized by population nu-dagger. It is not a conditional bootstrap theorem centered at theta-hat. Theorem 3 uses theta-hat and population V-dagger. The later Monte Carlo variance estimate is a different object.

The sparse model uses R_+^p together with a zero minimum, so nonnegativity must include zero here. Its residual parameters can be signed. The source does not define max over an empty support, although the sparsity conditions alone allow empty support.

The norm display following (6.2) omits the inactive coordinates xi/2. In particular it claims o(log p) when omega_1=2omega_2, even though omega_1>0 and inactive nodes yield order log p. This asserted identity is not treated as a separate definition or condition.

Theorem 4 does not assume the dense-model Condition 1 or give a sparse bootstrap central limit theorem. The preceding section explicitly describes a limited sparse extension. Dense assumptions and bootstrap variance interfaces are excluded from its dependency closure.
The sparse estimates in (6.3) are unthresholded. They are not constrained to be nonnegative or to have support S, and the theorem does not promise support recovery.

Theorems 1/2 keep s fixed as p grows. Theorem 3 is p-dimensional. Theorem 4 uses s as the size of a potentially growing sparse support with s=o(p). These quantifiers are distinct despite reusing the letter s.

Inverse square roots of variance terms and triangle averaging require positive normalizations and p>=3. These hold eventually under the interior model restrictions for the intended population quantities, but the source does not supply arbitrary-value conventions for excluded finite cases.
Theorem 4 uses M(gamma,C_1) with a comma, whereas the class definition uses a semicolon. The same class is resolved from Section 3.3 while the printed theorem punctuation remains unchanged.

Definition 1 takes a supremum only where the denominator Q(Z|X)>0. For general kernels with unequal supports, this does not expressly compare the omitted zero-denominator case; the census retains the exact definition. The interior jittering kernel used by the Theorems has common full support.

References to proofs and variance estimates in the Appendix or embedded supplement were not followed. The pinned source is arXiv v2; equality of its statements to final journal wording has not been established.

ambient_resolution.shared: Finite node indices, indicators, cardinalities and max norm are defined in A1/A3; asymptotic comparisons in A2; N in A6. Expectations, variances, real powers, logarithms, diagonal matrices, transpose, Gaussian laws, convergence in distribution and ordinary deterministic/stochastic big-O use their standard meanings under the pinned graph-and-noise model. Matrix/vector inequalities in Theorem 3 are componentwise (lower orthants). No library-availability claim is made. Conditions uniform in p retain their fixed-constant scope.
ambient_resolution.1: p tends to infinity; fixed s and chosen distinct indices ell_1,...,ell_s, fixed C_1 and the three gamma regimes are bound in the theorem. D2 supplies theta, D4 the admissible privacy pair, D5 Condition 1, D8 the original moment estimate and D10 the two population variance components. N=(p-1)(p-2), diag and the standard s-dimensional Gaussian resolve the normalizations. The extra script-I membership remains unresolved source wording (S1).
ambient_resolution.2: The opening reference supplies the dense beta-model, admissible privacy pair and Condition 1 from Theorem 1, without conjoining its alternative regimes. Fixed s and its indices are bound again. Delta and c are bound in this theorem; gamma follows its own stated window and A7. D14 is the bootstrap estimator; D16 supplies nu-dagger, D11 supplies nu in part (b). Original theta is the center; no conditional expectation or empirical variance normalization is substituted.
ambient_resolution.3: Theorem-bound delta and gamma sequences obey the displayed stronger restrictions. D2/D4/D5 give the dense model and assumptions, D8/A8 the original estimator vector, and D16 nu-dagger. V-dagger is defined inside the theorem as its diagonal matrix, xi is bound there as a p-dimensional standard Gaussian, and u ranges over R^p. The probabilities are unconditional lower-orthant probabilities, not bootstrap empirical CDFs.
ambient_resolution.4: D17 supplies xi, check-theta, S, s and the logarithmic reparametrization with little-o residuals; D18 supplies both sparse estimates via D8. D4 supplies M and gamma; omega_1,omega_2 and chi_p are restricted/defined in the theorem. D19 fixes the nonstandard tilde-O_p convention. The source chi_p parentheses and equality chain remain unresolved (S2/S3). No dense Condition 1, Gaussian approximation or bootstrap variance is inherited.
